verdict.supported_name_scope: Representative combined-mainstem river-system identity only; not a uniform name for every part
verdict.status: Supported representative combined-system identity; a uniform Frankland River name for the entire group is not supported.
verdict.identity_confidence: High for representative system and broad course association; exact headwater and reach-name boundaries unresolved.
verdict.scope: Existing selected baseline group, not a complete basin inventory or a uniform label for all parts.
verdict.korean_note: No direct Korean naming evidence acquired.

geometry_integrity.review_note: All decoded parts were included in the complete-route view and count, bounds, continuity and hash checks. Matching counts alone do not verify the original source-to-rendered-part crosswalk.

spatial_identity_check.method: Side-by-side visual review of all decoded baseline parts against complete regional, catchment, surveyed-section and estuary map views. No georegistered overlay or exact line fit.
spatial_identity_check.regional_course_comparison: The full baseline starts near 117.502,-33.825, bends southeast then west around latitude -34.2, and continues southwest before turning toward the coastal estuary. The distinctive middle bend agrees visually with the Gordon-labelled section in WRM44 Figure 6.3; the wider route is consistent with the regional and catchment maps.
spatial_identity_check.headwater_limit: The northern starting extension is outside the detailed surveyed-section map; its exact local name is unresolved. Regional system membership does not assign a name to every headwater.
spatial_identity_check.name_transition_limit: Gordon and Frankland are distinct component names. The documented transition north of Muir Highway has no verified selected-part or source-reach boundary.
spatial_identity_check.coastal_limit: Estuary context supports association with Nornalup Inlet; neither the inlet nor a terminal connector inherits the river name. Exact river/inlet and inlet/ocean boundaries are unverified.

outlet_scope.regional_receiving_water: Nornalup Inlet, within the Walpole-Nornalup estuarine system
outlet_scope.endpoint_interpretation: The retained source endpoint and rendered endpoint are distinct historical-baseline facts. Sea-terminal metadata does not establish a direct open-ocean mouth or the name of the terminal connector.

remaining_limits: Representative combined-system identity is supported, while whole-group scalar and per-reach naming remain false.
Exact headwater, Gordon/Frankland transition and river/inlet boundaries require finer authoritative evidence and a verified reach crosswalk.
Current deployment and original continental HydroRIVERS coordinate equality remain unverified.
